historical_growth.growth_rate_source: FY2027 base-case adjusted-net-revenue growth from the FY2026 guidance run-rate (+9.5-10%), record backlog $28.9B (+27% y/y, 1.2x TTM adj-net-revenue book-to-bill) and management's FY29 framework; NOT from the historical CAGRs, which are broken by the Sep-2024 Critical Mission Solutions separation (Amentum) and the Mar-2026 PA Consulting buy-in
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGRs (-15.8% 3yr, -9.0% 5yr) diverge by far more than 30pp from revenue (+7.1% 3yr) because the FY2024 Amentum spin distributed ~$2B of equity to shareholders and FY2025 carried Amentum mark-to-market losses; EPS CAGRs carry the same items (FY2025 GAAP EPS $2.39 vs adjusted $6.03). None of the book-value or EPS CAGRs describe the continuing business. Revenue CAGR uses gross revenue from the CSV (FY2022 restated continuing 9,783 -> FY2025 12,030); the FY2020 base (13,567) still includes the divested CMS business, hence the negative 5-year figure.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - equity-award taxes; interest income not stripped, net-debt company): FY2020 612.6, FY2021 551.5, FY2022 265.1, FY2023 738.7, FY2024 817.7, FY2025 519.1. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR (25.1%) exceeds reported (20.5%) only because the FY2022 base was depressed by working capital while SBC was flat -- not because SBC is shrinking; FY2025 owner FCF fell 37% on PA/separation working-capital drag. SBC at 1.0-1.1% of net revenue is small and stable -- reported growth is not being paid for in stock.

scenario_narratives.base: Backlog-led growth on the net-revenue base decelerating from 8% to 2.5% over ten years, with the adjusted EBITDA margin reaching ~16% (pre-SBC 17%) by FY31 -- management's FY29 target, two years late -- and staying there. Buybacks keep the diluted count flat at 118.2M; net debt of $2.4B from the PA Consulting buy-in is deducted once. The house value lands close to the current price, i.e. the market is paying roughly base-case fair value.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI-infrastructure, semiconductor and life-sciences capex cycle runs through FY29 with visibility into FY28 already booked, PA Consulting synergies and mix lift margins to 18% pre-SBC, and growth stays at or above 8% for four years. Requires both continued hyperscaler capital spending and successful PA integration -- two independent things going right.
scenario_narratives.bear: An AI-capex pause in FY27-28 plus slower public-sector awards leaves net revenue roughly flat for two years; margins compress ~150bp on utilization and wage inflation and never regain the FY26 level; the stock re-rates to a cyclical E&C multiple. The balance sheet ($2.4B net debt, ~1.7x FY26 adjusted EBITDA, no near-term maturities after the 2026 refinancing) survives this path comfortably; the loss is valuation, not solvency.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Jacobs as an asset-light professional-services compounder on its own adjusted-net-revenue basis, charging SBC in full and holding the share count flat, taxing at the 26% adjusted rate, and haircutting adjusted EBITDA for the restructuring and transaction costs that recur every year. The margin path is anchored to the FY26 guidance and management's FY29 framework but reaches the latter later than management does. Net debt from the PA Consulting buy-in, the deferred PA consideration and the after-tax pension deficit are deducted once. The 15% hurdle entry price is the buy-below figure; the WACC-based intrinsic value is the fair-value figure. SANITY CHECK (2026-09-29): the implied-P/E rule tripped at 77x vs 2x the 10-year average of 33x. That is a denominator artefact, not an overvaluation signal, and no driver was changed. The checker divides by trailing GAAP EPS less SBC/share (FY2025 GAAP EPS $2.39, ~$1.97 after SBC), and FY2025 GAAP EPS carries the Amentum-stake mark-to-market losses and separation costs from the Sep-2024 spin-off; the FY2026 GAAP quarters add the PA Consulting buy-in charges ($237.5M vested subsidiary compensation, $123.9M consideration treated as compensation, a 43% GAAP tax rate in Q3). Jacobs' adjusted EPS was $6.03 in FY2025 and is guided at $7.20-7.30 for FY2026. On the $7.25 midpoint the weighted IV of ~$152 is 21.0x (23.8x after deducting SBC of ~$0.86/share, the checker's basis) and the current price is ~19x; the historical 33x average is itself lifted by two one-off years (FY2018 73x on CH2M acquisition costs and the Tax Act charge, FY2025 66x on the Amentum MTM) and averages 24x without them, so the valuation sits on the historical mean, not at double it. The other rules corroborate: implied EV/EBITDA 22.3x vs a 21.9x average and P/Sales 1.6x vs 1.0x (net-revenue mix and margin higher post-spin), and at the weighted IV the enterprise value is ~14.7x FY2026 guided adjusted EBITDA. The 'growth too high' diagnosis compares an 8% adjusted-net-revenue growth path with a 2% through-cycle gross-revenue CAGR whose FY2020 base still contains the divested Critical Mission Solutions business and whose gross line carries 28-37% zero-margin pass-throughs -- neither the numerator nor the denominator is the series being projected. Step 8c.5 options (mid-cycle FCF, WACC premium, growth cap) do not address the cause: FY0 is guidance not a peak, the WACC is built from current USD rates, and the growth path already decays to 2.5%; an 18x/20x/14x exit-multiple cap is already in place and is non-binding in the base case (Gordon 17.1x FCF, ~10.9x terminal EV/EBITDA). Investment framing: the market is paying roughly base-case fair value (weighted IV ~10% above price); the 15% hurdle entry price is the buy-below level, and the real risk is the AI/data-center capex cycle in the bear path, not the multiple.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI/data-center capex cycle turning before FY28: the bear path removes roughly a third of the base value
Pass-through mix: gross revenue is not the driver -- if pass-through share keeps rising, reported revenue growth will overstate net-revenue growth (already 34% vs 8% in Q3 FY26)
Working capital: receivables/contract assets consumed $595M in 9M FY26 (offset by payables); a reversal of the payables build would depress reported FCF for a year
Margin target risk: the 17% pre-SBC terminal margin (adjusted ~16%) is above any year Jacobs has yet delivered; the bear case holds 15%
FY26 Q4 cash flow and Q4 buybacks are not in the June balance sheet -- refresh net debt and share count at the November 10-K

sanity_check_fix.fix_applied: none to drivers -- documented false positive from denominator distortion (FY2025 GAAP EPS $2.39 carries Amentum MTM/separation costs; FY2026 GAAP carries PA Consulting buy-in charges). fiscal_year_end made machine-readable ('26 September') so the checker stops falling back to December.
sanity_check_fix.implied_pe_on_adjusted_eps: weighted IV / FY2026 guided adjusted EPS $7.25 = 21.0x; SBC-adjusted (7.25-0.86) = 23.8x; historical average ex FY2018/FY2025 outliers = 24.1x

inputs.revenue_basis: ADJUSTED NET REVENUE (gross revenue less pass-through subcontract/procurement billings), FY2026E = FY2025 actual 8,695.0 x 1.0975 (guidance midpoint). Gross revenue (the Metrics.csv 'Revenue' column, FY2025 12,029.8; 9M FY2026 11,064.6) carries 28-37% of zero-margin pass-throughs whose mix swung +34% y/y in FY2026, so every margin, guidance figure and FY29 target Jacobs publishes is on the net basis. Modelled on that basis; do not compare projected revenue with the CSV gross line.
inputs.share_count_basis: 117.04M basic at 2026-07-24 (10-Q Q3 FY2026 cover) + 1.15M dilutive stock-compensation shares (Q3 FY2026 EPS table, three-month column) = 118.2M fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). The 2.04M shares issued for PA Consulting on 2026-03-20 are already in the count. Buybacks of $614M in 9M FY2026 fund the flat count and more; the count is being paid for, not assumed.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026E: 9M FY2026 10-Q cash-flow statement SBC add-back $56.9M + Q4 run-rate ~$15M (FY2025 Q4 was $13.6M) = ~$72M; taxes paid on vested restricted stock $29.2M in 9M (vesting is Q1-Q2 seasonal; FY2025 full year $27.45M vs 9M $27.0M) = ~$30M. Jacobs publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure and does NOT add SBC back in its adjusted earnings, so the two lines are summed. FY2025 actuals for reference: SBC $60.96M, equity-award taxes $27.45M, total $88.4M (Metrics.csv / kpis). Excluded from SBC: the $237.5M of PA Consulting 'subsidiary level compensation based agreements' that vested on the buy-in and the $123.9M of consideration treated as compensation -- both one-off, closed with the transaction.
inputs.buyback_note: 9M FY2026 common stock repurchases $614.1M (10-Q financing activities); FY2025 $754.1M; FY2024 $402.7M. Actual cash, not authorization.
inputs.fy0_basis: FY2026 (52 weeks to 2026-09-25) closed four days before the valuation date and is unreported; FY0 is built from FY2025 actuals x the 2026-08-04 guidance (adj net revenue +9.5-10.0%, adj EBITDA margin 14.7-14.8%, adj FCF margin ~8%), of which 9 months are in the 10-Q. Year 1 of the forecast is FY2027. Q4 FY2026 free cash flow (Jul-Sep 2026, roughly $150-350M) is not in the June balance sheet and not in the flows -- a ~$1.5-3/share understatement, left as conservatism rather than estimated.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2026E adjusted FCF at the ~8% guided margin on 9,543 net revenue = ~$763M (company definition: OCF less capex, excluding the $342M 9M payout of PA transaction proceeds to PA employees, which is one-off). This is a LEVERED figure (after ~$190M of interest paid); the forward build is unlevered from adjusted EBITDA and reconciles: 763 + after-tax interest ~140 + ~40 recurring restructuring cash costs ~= 940 reported-basis unlevered, vs the component build's FY0-equivalent ~975 before SBC. FY2025 actual reported FCF $607.5M (7.0% of net revenue); owner FCF FY2025 = 607.5 - 88.4 = $519.1M.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST, Sep-2026), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.05 -> cost of equity ~9.5%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.3% (4.75%/5.375% bonds issued Mar-2026, 5.90% 2033 bonds, 2026 term loans) -> ~3.9% after tax. Weights at market: equity 118.2M shares at the price in current_price = ~$16.4B market cap, debt $3.6B -> 18% debt. WACC = 0.82 x 9.5 + 0.18 x 3.9 = 8.5%, used in all three scenarios (risk is charged once, via scenario weights).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (office space; ROU assets $311M, liabilities $475M at 2026-06-26). Lease cost sits in SG&A, i.e. inside adjusted EBITDA, so it is charged in the flows; lease liabilities are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt. One treatment, never both.
inputs.nci_treatment: Redeemable NCI (the ~35% of PA Consulting) was eliminated by the 2026-03-20 buy-in; the residual consolidated-JV NCI is a $13.8M deficit at 2026-06-26 and is ignored. Flows are 100% attributable from FY0 onward. The £75M deferred PA consideration payable in FY2028 (accrued in other deferred liabilities) is deducted in the equity bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (margins still ramping toward the FY29 framework in year 5). Jacobs is a US-listed, USD-reporting, asset-light professional-services operating company (engineering, program management, PA Consulting advisory) -- the SKILL.md routing table's first row. Not a bank/REIT/holdco; no dual currency; NCI gone since Mar-2026; leases inside EBITDA. Section 7 adaptations file not needed. EBITDA PATH IS PRE-SBC: Jacobs' adjusted EBITDA is stated AFTER stock compensation (SBC is not one of its non-GAAP add-backs), so ebitda_margin_path = adjusted EBITDA margin + SBC% - ~0.45pp for restructuring/transaction cash costs that recur every year ($47M in 9M FY2025, $40M in 9M FY2026) but are excluded from 'adjusted'. Engine then deducts sbc_pct_path to arrive back at a house EBITDA ~0.5pp below Jacobs' adjusted figure. D&A path is PP&E depreciation only (FY2025 $82.1M = 0.94% of net revenue); intangible amortization ($155.5M FY2025, non-cash, excluded from adjusted EBITDA) is not deducted; its tax shield is small and ignored. Cash tax 26% = FY2025/Q3 FY2026 adjusted effective rate (26.5%/26.4%); the 43% GAAP rate in Q3 FY2026 is a PA-transaction artefact. Working capital: receivables + contract assets 3,761 - contract liabilities 1,020 - payables 1,778 = ~$963M net investment (~10% of net revenue), so wc_capture is NEGATIVE 10% of the change in net revenue -- growth consumes cash. Interest income ($35.8M FY2025) is NOT stripped: Jacobs is a net-debt company (net debt 2.6x FY0 owner FCF) so the cash pile is not double-counted; the unlevered build never includes it anyway. Price is the 2026-09-28 regular close; 52-week range 105.68-168.44.
inputs.fiscal_year_end_note: 52/53-week year ending the last Friday of September (FY2025 ended 2025-09-26, FY2026 ends 2026-09-25). Bare day-month kept in fiscal_year_end so the multiples checker keys historical periods to September, not its December fallback.

bear.narrative: Hyperscaler capex digestion in FY27-28 stalls the fastest-growing 11%+ of net revenue while public transportation/water awards slip on budget cycles; utilization falls and engineering wage inflation is not fully passed through, so the pre-SBC margin dips to 14.2% (adjusted ~13%) before recovering only to 15% -- below the FY26 level, i.e. the FY29 framework is never met. Cap 14x: the market re-rates Jacobs back to a cyclical E&C multiple.

base.narrative: FY27 growth 8% steps down from the ~9.75% FY26 run-rate as the pass-through-light net-revenue base compounds on backlog already booked (visibility into 2027-28 on AI/data-center work), then decays to 2.5% by year 10. Pre-SBC EBITDA margin 15.8% -> 17.0% by FY31 (adjusted-basis ~16.0-16.5% after SBC and the recurring-restructuring haircut), i.e. reaching management's FY29 '16%+' framework two years late and holding there. Cap 18x FCF: a mature, asset-light professional-services compounder.

bull.narrative: The AI/data-center and semiconductor build-out keeps compounding through FY29 (pipeline up ~400% y/y, direct AI work rising ~100bp of mix per quarter), water and life-sciences capital programs stay non-discretionary, and PA Consulting cross-sell plus $20M+ synergies lift the pre-SBC margin to 18% (adjusted ~17%), beating the FY29 framework. Double-digit net-revenue growth for three years, then a slower decay.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because 11% and rising of net revenue is direct AI/data-center work whose durability is a live 2026 debate, the stock has re-rated on that theme, and FY2025 already showed how far owner FCF can swing on working capital (-37%). Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs the AI cycle, PA Consulting integration and margin expansion to all deliver at once. No going-concern or covenant risk: leverage ~1.7x adjusted EBITDA and the debt was termed out in March 2026.
